title: A wrapped label says which width you are looking at
goal: When a label is too wide for the box holding it, the app breaks it onto more lines and narrows it to fit. Its width then reads as the room the box had, not as how wide its own words are, and the two numbers look like they disagree with each other. A person building to a spec cannot tell which one they are reading.
notes: Comes out of a-stretched-piece-stops-offering-a-size-you-cann (2026-09-06), which was asked to make this a readout and found the premise false. Evidence, verified with a test: a label with natural width 166 inside a 100-wide free group flows to 104 with wrappedByItsContainer = true. Typing 60 or 140 CLEARS the flag in Layer.resized and sticks; only 400 (wider than the words) snaps back to 104, because textHugsItsWords is then true again and GroupFlow.wrapping re-wraps it. So the W field is a live control, not a decided number, and it must NOT become a GeometryReadout: that would remove the keyboard way to set a paragraph width while the canvas drag keeps it. The real complaint is the audit line 2026-09-05-words-that-wrap rough3: two numbers that look like they disagree. Likely answers are a word in the Layout section rather than a change to the W field. Ask the user before building: this is a visual-direction call.
acceptance: The width shown for a label the container wrapped is unambiguous: it is clear whether it is the room the container gave it or how wide the words themselves are
Typing a width into a wrapped label still works exactly as it does today, because it does work: anything at or below the words own width sticks and makes it a paragraph, the same as dragging its edge
A label nothing has wrapped is unchanged
A screenshot in the audit shows a wrapped label beside its number

log.note: Adversarial review before building: reproduced the complaint rather than trusting it, and found the premise is TRUE but mis-stated. Core repro (throwaway test): a label whose words are 141 wide, inside a free group with Largest width 100, comes out with a frame of 100 while the WRAPPED words only reach 78. Same for two other phrases (104 natural, 100 box, 63 ink; 151 natural, 100 box, 89 ink). textWrapped(inRoom:) sets the frame to the whole room the container allowed, not to the longest line the wrap produced.

Reproduced live in the probe app too, with Screen Recording granted. Scripts/playtest/wrapped-label-width-walk.json builds the audit's own example: a square and the words Save all the changes, stacked, Largest width 140, then picks the LABEL. Capture wrapped-2-label-sc.png: the label's selection outline runs the full 140 while the longest line stops about 29 short of it, and W reads 140. So the two numbers that look like they disagree are the label's W and the words a person can see.

Checked the ripple before proposing a change: GroupFlow.placed decides the group's width from the UNWRAPPED children, then wraps, then only re-measures height. Verified: a group with Largest 100 holding a label whose wrapped ink is 78 comes out 100. So narrowing the label to its words does not on its own narrow the group; a group that hugs would stay at its ceiling with a visible gap unless it is re-measured after the wrap too. That is the part a person should decide, so it went into the decision rather than being guessed.

Shortest version considered and rejected: turning W into a readout. The predecessor task already proved that removes the only keyboard way to set a paragraph width while the canvas drag keeps it. Stretched and filled labels are untouched either way, since GroupFlow.wrapRooms excludes them and they keep going through sizeIsDecidedByItsContainer.

Waiting on a visual-direction decision: after a wrap, should a label be as wide as the words that came out, or as wide as the room it was given? Reproduced both in a test and live in the probe app, with a capture in the brief.
decision "When words are wrapped to fit the box around them, should the label be as wide as the words that came out, or as wide as the room it was given?" resolved: Fit the words

Adversarial review before building: the decision was already answered (Fit the words), so the question was whether it is safe. Two things could have broken it. (1) Would re-wrapping at the longest line move the breaks? No: every line already fits that width, and the word that would not fit the wider room does not fit the narrower one either, so the breaks are identical and the flow settles in one pass. (2) Does the REAL CoreText measurement return the ink width or the width you asked for? Ink: CTFramesetterSuggestFrameSizeWithConstraints returns the longest line. Checked with a throwaway test that installed TextRasterizer.naturalSize into TextMeasurement, the way the app does at launch: Save all the changes at 24pt is 216 natural; in a column stack capped at 140 the label came out 122 (content 118) and the stack settled at 118, identical on passes two and three.

Shipped in 6bf24960. Layer.textWrapped(inRoom:) takes the measured width of the lines it produced, floored at the widest single word so an unbreakable word still overhangs at its own width. GroupFlow.placed measures the group again across after the wrap, but ONLY where the width was a limit on an axis that hugs, so a typed width and a floor are both untouched. Six new tests in GroupTextWrapTests (wrapped label hugs its words, hugging group settles, floor still holds, typed group width kept, typed label width sticks through a pass, nested stack settles in one pass) and six existing ones updated to the decided behaviour. Full Scripts/test.sh: 8059 tests green apart from one unrelated timing flake (logged on timing-budget-tests-pass-reliably-on-a-busy-mach).

Acceptance item 4 (a screenshot beside the number) could NOT be met: the Mac's screen was locked for the whole task, so Scripts/playtest.sh wrapped-label-width-walk.json reported status locked, exit 3, 0 steps, and no walk can run or photograph anything. What shipped instead is an offscreen render from the app's own renderer (queue/audits/2026-09-17-wrapped-label-width.png), drawn with three boxes so the room the ceiling allowed (140), the stack that settled (121) and the label's box (89) are all visible at once, and the audit says in rough that it is a render and not a photograph of the window. The walk itself was rewritten to describe and look for the new behaviour; it needs an unlocked screen to run.

left rough: a centred label inside a wrapped box now centres its lines in the narrower box rather than the room, so an existing canvas can move by a couple of points. Looked right in every render and in the tests, so it did not earn a task. Also left rough: the stack's own W and its Largest width now show different numbers a row apart, which is the answered decision working, but it is the one place two numbers could still be read as disagreeing. The nested-stack overhang found while testing DID clear the bar and is filed as words-inside-a-stack-inside-a-capped-stack-hang.

Asked for a full sweep: this change touches every group that has a width and a label in it, so any walk with a capped stack or a typed group width could shift by a few points, and the rewritten wrapped-label-width walk has never run. Not waited on.

A wrapped label now takes the width of the lines it produced, not the room it was allowed (Layer.textWrapped), and a group whose width was a LIMIT measures itself again after the wrap so it settles around the wrapped words (GroupFlow.placed). Shipped in 6bf24960 with 6 new and 6 updated tests; full Scripts/test.sh green at 8059 tests bar one unrelated timing flake. Verified with the real CoreText measurement as well as the test estimate: 216 natural at 24pt, 118 wrapped in a stack capped at 140, identical over three passes. Not seen in the running app: the screen was locked all task, so no walk could run and the audit ships an offscreen render and says so.
